interpretation: The post-handoff amplitude sweep exposed a monotone Jpk/width tradeoff rather than a joint-safe solution. At second_amp=-0.0145, worst Jpk improved to +0.105750% but peak width fell to +0.017869%; at -0.0160, peak width crossed the frozen +0.020% gate at +0.020580% but worst Jpk worsened to +0.114205%. No case was current-safe or sustained-safe, and the critical excursion remained at t=0.14 with minimum width near t=0.16. This supports a focused coupled timing/amplitude test: move the handoff earlier to create Jpk margin while retaining stronger post-handoff drive, rather than extending the one-dimensional amplitude sweep.
claim_boundary: Normalized native M3D-C1 uninterrupted two-profile amplitude refinement only; frozen +0.020% width and +0.10% Jpk gates unchanged; no reactor-scale or experimental stabilization claim.
new_job_rationale: Sweep handoff t=0.07, 0.08, 0.09 against second-stage amplitudes -0.0155, -0.0160, -0.0165 while holding geometry and first-stage drive fixed, testing whether additional preemption buys enough Jpk margin to recover joint authority without relaxing either frozen gate.
